page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n4d server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration does not include any bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The instance utilizes dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring that compute resources are not shared with other tenants. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached block storage. Additionally, the low memory-to-CPU ratio of 1:2 positions this instance specifically for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints.

Due to the 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB RAM configuration, the n4d-highcpu-8 is designed for compute-intensive tasks. Suitable workloads include batch processing, distributed analytics, web serving, and lightweight containerized applications that require dedicated CPU cycles but have modest memory requirements.
